messages.content:
Return a complete version 2b1 ordered block envelope using the supplied JSON schema. Use text blocks for prose. At most one ui block contains only the requested protocol source and initial integer state entries (empty uses defaults). No fences. No JavaScript, tools, events, HTML or links. One Stack with unique named leaves. Up to 40 leaves, 40 collection members, 64 declarations, depth 32, 16000 UTF-8 source bytes, 10000 frame bytes. Integers for input state. Names start with ASCII letter, then alphanumeric or underscore, at most 48 characters. All declarations must be reachable. Text and labels at most 512 characters. Safe Graphic items use kind plus only required fields: rect(x,y,width,height), circle(cx,cy,r), text(x,y,text), path(d using only M L H V Z, lowercase equivalents, numbers, spaces or commas), group(items of leaves). Numeric coordinates 0..640; viewBox 0 0 450 135.
One assignment per physical line. root = Stack([leafName, otherLeaf]). Each leaf is one named call: Text("text"), Metric("label",numericValue), Control("label",literalMin,literalMax,choices,$variable), Table([{label:"name",score:number}]), Graphic("label",items). Declare $variable = integer and bind it to exactly one Control. Use [] for range or literal string options indexed 0..n-1. Derived name = expression. Strings use double quotes. Numeric + - * /, == > <, condition ? yes : no, arrays, objects, named references, @Sum(numbers), @Sort(rows,"score","desc") are allowed. No unary minus, concatenation, member access, map, interpolation or inline nested components. Produce complete root and definitions.
Choose text for a simple definition. Use a legible diagram if spatial relationships aid understanding. Use controls for a changing decision. Label units, state assumptions, use short readable labels, give each output an informative name and check zero or boundary conditions. Keep geometry inside the viewBox.
Treat the request as the complete source of domain rules. Include exactly its input dimensions, options, units, defaults and ranges. Check that each input changes the intended outputs. Do not invent extra tiers, exceptions or fees. Interpret terminology in its application context. Provide an actual interaction when requested. Do not claim a visible control exists in prose alone.

Build an interactive weighted comparison of Native Hybrid [9,8,7], Tauri [7,8,8], and Electron [6,4,10]. The three criteria are native experience, lightweight runtime, delivery efficiency. Start with integer weights 40,25,35. Normalize by their sum, rank descending, and show no ranking if all weights are zero. Scores are synthetic.

attempts.raw:
{"version":"2b1","blocks":[{"type":"ui","source":"// Weighted comparison of Native Hybrid, Tauri, and Electron frameworks
// Criteria: Native Experience, Lightweight Runtime, Delivery Efficiency
// Initial weights: 40, 25, 35
// Scores: Native Hybrid [9,8,7], Tauri [7,8,8], Electron [6,4,10]

$weight_native = 40
$weight_light = 25
$weight_delivery = 35

weight_sum = $weight_native + $weight_light + $weight_delivery

norm_native = weight_sum == 0 ? 0 : $weight_native / weight_sum
norm_light = weight_sum == 0 ? 0 : $weight_light / weight_sum
norm_delivery = weight_sum == 0 ? 0 : $weight_delivery / weight_sum

scores = [
  {name:"Native Hybrid", native:9, light:8, delivery:7},
  {name:"Tauri", native:7, light:8, delivery:8},
  {name:"Electron", native:6, light:4, delivery:10}
]

weighted_scores = [
  {name:"Native Hybrid", score: scores[0].native*norm_native + scores[0].light*norm_light + scores[0].delivery*norm_delivery},
  {name:"Tauri", score: scores[1].native*norm_native + scores[1].light*norm_light + scores[1].delivery*norm_delivery},
  {name:"Electron", score: scores[2].native*norm_native + scores[2].light*norm_light + scores[2].delivery*norm_delivery}
]

sorted_scores = @Sort(weighted_scores,"score","desc")

ranking_labels = weight_sum == 0 ? ["","",""] : ["1","2","3"]

ranking_table = [
  {name:sorted_scores[0].name, score:sorted_scores[0].score, rank:ranking_labels[0]},
  {name:sorted_scores[1].name, score:sorted_scores[1].score, rank:ranking_labels[1]},
  {name:sorted_scores[2].name, score:sorted_scores[2].score, rank:ranking_labels[2]}
]

Control("Native Experience Weight",0,100,[],$weight_native)
Control("Lightweight Runtime Weight",0,100,[],$weight_light)
Control("Delivery Efficiency Weight",0,100,[],$weight_delivery)

Table(ranking_table)","state":[{"name":"weight_native","value":40},{"name":"weight_light","value":25},{"name":"weight_delivery","value":35}]},{"type":"text","text":"Weighted Comparison of Frameworks

Adjust the weights for each criterion using the sliders above to see how the overall ranking changes.

Criteria:
- Native Experience: How close the framework feels to native platform capabilities.
- Lightweight Runtime: The efficiency and small footprint of the runtime environment.
- Delivery Efficiency: Ease and speed of delivering updates and builds.

Weights are normalized to sum 1. Rankings show the order of frameworks by weighted score.

Scores for frameworks by criterion:
- Native Hybrid: Native Experience 9, Lightweight Runtime 8, Delivery Efficiency 7
- Tauri: Native Experience 7, Lightweight Runtime 8, Delivery Efficiency 8
- Electron: Native Experience 6, Lightweight Runtime 4, Delivery Efficiency 10

All scores are on a 0-10 scale.

Weighted score = sum of (criterion score × normalized weight).

Ranking Table shows the framework names, their weighted scores, and ranks.

If all weights are zero, no ranking is shown."}]}
